title: Find the Percent of a Number
contentObjective: I can find the percent of a number using an equation or a model.
languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words percent, base, part, and equation.

noticeAndWonder.context: Before we head to Discount Day at the arcade, warm up with a percent of a number. This storage bar shows part of a whole, just like a percent-off deal shows part of a ticket price. Approximately what percent of the storage is used? If the phone holds 200 GB, about how many gigabytes is that percent of the whole?
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Food Drive
revealWordProblem.text: The organizers of a food drive set a new goal for a second food drive. They hope to collect 140% as many cans as they did for the last food drive in which they collected 145 cans. About how many cans can the organizers expect to collect? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Change 140% to its decimal form: 140% = 1.40. Multiply the decimal by the base: 1.40 × 145 = 203. The organizers can expect to collect about 203 cans for the second food drive.

turnAndTalk.question: On Discount Day the claw machine is 25% off its 60-ticket price. In '25% of 60,' which number is the base (the whole), and what part are you trying to find?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The base is 60 tickets and the part is the 25% discount we need to find.

stems.en: The base is ___ and the part I want is ___.
stems.es: La base es ___ y la parte que quiero es ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students identify 60 as the base, the 25% discount as the part to find, and connect 'of' to the base.
turnAndTalk.extend: Without computing exactly, will the discount be more or less than half of 60? Use a benchmark to estimate and explain.
extendStems: The discount will be ___ than half because ___.

turnAndTalk.question: What steps did you follow every time to find the percent of a number in the discount table?
turnAndTalk.kernel: I changed the percent to a decimal, then multiplied it by the base to get the part.
turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students describe the equation part = percent x base, converting the percent to a decimal first (e.g., 0.40 x 80 = 32).
turnAndTalk.extend: Compare finding 25% of 60 with the decimal 0.25 versus dividing 60 into 4 equal parts. Why do both methods give the same part?
extendStems: Both give ___ because 25% is the same as ___.

turnAndTalk.question: The arcade donates 12% of Saturday's 1,500 ticket sales. The manager says 180 tickets, a student says 18. Who is right, and how do you know?
turnAndTalk.kernel: 12% of 1,500 is 0.12 times 1,500, which is 180 tickets.

stems.en: The ___ is correct because 12% of 1,500 = ___ x 1,500 = ___.
stems.es: El/La ___ tiene razón porque 12% de 1,500 = ___ x 1,500 = ___.

stems.en: The mistake was using ___ instead of ___.
stems.es: El error fue usar ___ en lugar de ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students compute 0.12 x 1,500 = 180 and explain the student likely used 0.012 (divided by 1,000) instead of 0.12.
turnAndTalk.extend: Estimate first: 10% of 1,500 is easy to find. Use that to check whether 180 is reasonable for 12%, and explain your reasoning.
extendStems: 10% of 1,500 is ___, so 12% should be a little ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Find the Percent of a Number, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: To find the part, change the percent to a decimal, then multiply: part = percent × base.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.AT.4 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

visual.title: Discount Day: Two Arcade Deals
visual.caption: Which game's deal shades off a bigger slice of its full price — and about how much of the whole bar is that?

launch.narrative: It's Discount Day at the arcade! Different games are offering percent-off deals on ticket prices. The claw machine is 25% off its usual 60-ticket price, and the racing game is 40% off 80 tickets. You need to calculate the discounts to figure out how many tickets each game actually costs!
launch.contextImage: Arcade games with colorful discount signs showing various percent-off deals
noticePrompts: What information do you need to find the discount amount?
How is finding 25% of 60 different from finding 40% of 80?
wonderPrompts: Is there more than one way to find a percent of a number?
How does a bar model help you see the percent of a number?

conceptIntro.heading: How do I find the percent of a number?
conceptIntro.intro: The base is the whole amount. The part is the piece you get when you take a percent of the base. The word "of" tells you to multiply.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To find the part, change the percent to a decimal, then multiply: part = percent × base.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: The claw machine is 25% off its 60-ticket price. I want the discount.
First I change 25% to a decimal: 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25.
Then I multiply by the base: 0.25 × 60 = 15.
So the discount is 15 tickets. The part is 15.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's find 40% of 80. What is 40% as a decimal? (0.40)

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: In the table, change each percent to a decimal, then multiply by the base.
Find the discount amount for each arcade game.

explore.instructions: Find the percent of each number. Use the equation: Part = Percent × Base. Convert the percent to a decimal first.

discourse.prompt: What steps do you follow every time you find the percent of a number?
discourse.sentenceFrame: To find ___% of ___, I first convert the percent to ___, then I multiply ___ × ___ = ___.

optional.stem: The claw machine prize is 80 tickets and today it is 25% off. How many tickets do you save?
choiceFeedback: Find 25% of 80, then subtract from 80.
Did you find the discount amount and subtract correctly?
Check: 25% of 80 is how much off?

optional.stem: Your bowling score was 60 points. The bonus round adds 15% more points. How many bonus points is that?
choiceFeedback: Find 15% of 60, then add to the original score.
Did you add the bonus to the original correctly?
Check: 15% of 60 is how much bonus?

optional.stem: A snack at the arcade costs $40. The sales tax is 5%. How many dollars is the tax?
choiceFeedback: Find 5% of $40, then add to the original price.
Did you include both the price and the tax?
Check: 5% of $40 is how much tax?

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Discount Dash Color-by-Code Error
optional.correctWork: First change 20% to a decimal: 20 ÷ 100 = 0.20. Then multiply by the base: 0.20 × 50 = 10. So 20% of 50 = 10, not 20.
hints: A percent is not a whole number by itself — change 20% to a decimal before you multiply.
20% = 0.20. Then multiply 0.20 × 50 to find the part.

choiceFeedback: Multiply 150 by 0.20, or divide by 5.
Double-check your multiplication.
Try converting 20% to a decimal or fraction first.
hints: '20% of 150' means you want a PART of 150 — the answer should be smaller than 150.
Convert the percent to a decimal, then multiply: Part = Percent × Base.
Write 20% as 0.20, then set up 0.20 × 150. (Shortcut: 10% of 150 is 15 — double it.)

choiceFeedback: 50% is half — divide 84 by 2.
Check your calculation.
Remember: 50% means one-half.
hints: 50% is a friendly percent — it means exactly one-half of the number.
Finding 50% of a number is the same as dividing that number by 2.
Set up 84 ÷ 2, or check with the formula: 0.50 × 84.

approaching.explanation: 10% = 0.10. Multiply: 0.10 × 320 = 32. (Or move the decimal one place left.)
choiceFeedback: 10% is one-tenth — divide 320 by 10 or move the decimal.
Check: what is one-tenth of 320?
10% is easy: just divide by 10.
hints: 10% means one-tenth — there's a shortcut that needs no multiplication at all.
To find 10% of any number, move the decimal point one place to the left (divide by 10).
Start with 320 and slide the decimal one place left: 320 → what number?

choiceFeedback: Divide 15 by 50, then multiply by 100.
Set it up as a fraction: 15/50, then convert to a percent.
Find what fraction 15 is of 50, then convert.
hints: This question is backwards from the others: you have the part (15) and the whole (50), and you need the PERCENT.
Write the part over the whole as a fraction, then convert that fraction to a percent.
Set up 15/50. Divide 15 by 50 to get a decimal, then multiply by 100.

approaching.instructions: Find each percent of a number using the formula: Part = Percent × Base.
hints: The finished row shows the recipe: 25% of 60 became 0.25 × 60 = 15. Your rows use the same formula.
Convert each percent to a decimal, then multiply by the Base: Part = Percent × Base.
Row 2: write 40% as 0.40 and multiply 0.40 × 80. Then do 0.15 × 200 for the last row.

approaching.title: approaching — Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: First change the percent to a decimal: 30% = 30 ÷ 100 = 0.30. Then multiply by the base: 0.30 × 80 = 24. So 30% of 80 = 24, not 2,400. The student multiplied by 30 instead of 0.30.
hints: A percent is not a whole number — change 30% to a decimal before you multiply.
30% = 0.30. Multiply 0.30 × 80 to find the part: 24.

onLevel.instructions: Complete each row to find the percent of a number.
hints: Every row is the same job: find the percent OF the base. The Part should be smaller than the Base when the percent is under 100%.
Convert each percent to a decimal and multiply by the base. Shortcut: find 10% first, then scale.
Row 1: 10% of 250 — slide the decimal in 250 one place left. For 75% of 120, try 0.75 × 120 (or 3/4 of 120).

onLevel.stem: An arcade prize costs 240 tickets. If you have a coupon for 15% off, how many tickets do you save?
choiceFeedback: Find the discount amount, then subtract from the original.
Make sure you're subtracting the discount from the total.
Check: what is the discount, and what's left?
hints: Read carefully: the question asks how many tickets you SAVE — that's just the discount amount, not the new price.
The savings = 15% of the original 240 tickets. Convert 15% to a decimal and multiply.
Set up 0.15 × 240. (Shortcut: 10% of 240 is 24, and 5% is half of that — add them.)

onLevel.instructions: A game has 200 total points. Use the bar model to find 25% of 200.
onLevel.label: 200 ÷ 4 = 50. Each 25% section = 50 points. So 25% of 200 = 50.
hints: The bar shows 200 points cut into 4 equal sections, and each section is 25%.
Since 4 equal parts make the whole, one part = the whole divided by 4.
Divide 200 by 4 to find the value of one 25% section — that section IS 25% of 200.

onLevel.stem: A student scored 72 out of 90 on a test. What percent did they score?
choiceFeedback: Divide 72 by 90, then multiply by 100.
Convert to a fraction first: 72/90, then to a percent.
Find what fraction 72 is of 90, then convert to percent.
hints: The score 72 is the part and 90 is the whole — you need what percent 72 is OF 90.
Divide the part by the whole, then multiply the decimal by 100 to get the percent.
Set up 72 ÷ 90. (It may help to simplify 72/90 first — both divide by 9.)

onLevel.title: onLevel — Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Change the percent to a decimal

onLevel.correctWork: The base is 60, not 15. The word "of" tells you the base: 15% OF 60. Multiply by the base: 0.15 × 60 = 9. So 15% of 60 = 9, not 2.25. The student multiplied by the percent number instead of the base.
hints: What number comes after the word "of"? That is the base you multiply by.
15% = 0.15, and the base is 60. Multiply 0.15 × 60 = 9.

extending.title: Find the Percent Error
extending.correctWork: 30% = 0.30 (divide by 100, not by 10). 0.30 × 90 = 27. The correct answer is 27.
hints: To convert a percent to a decimal, divide by 100 — how many places does the decimal move?
30% = 0.30, not 3.0. The student divided by 10 instead of 100.

extending.prompt: A class has 32 students. 25% are in the math club, 50% are in the reading club, and 12.5% are in both. How many students are in each group? Can the total of all three groups be more than 32? Explain why or why not.
extending.sentenceFrame: There are ___ in math club, ___ in reading club, and ___ in both. The total ___ be more than 32 because ___.
extending.hint: Find how many students ARE in at least one club, then subtract from the total to find how many are NOT in either club.
hints: There are three separate percents of the SAME 32 students: 25%, 50%, and 12.5%. Find each group first.
Use friendly fractions: 25% = 1/4, 50% = 1/2, and 12.5% = 1/8. Then think about students who got counted in two groups.
Start with 25% of 32: that's 32 ÷ 4. Then do 32 ÷ 2 and 32 ÷ 8, and think about the 'both clubs' overlap.

extending.instructions: A video game character starts with 500 health points. Complete the table to find how many health points are lost or gained.
hints: Watch the words 'of current' — each row uses the health from the row above it, not the original 500.
For each event: percent → decimal, multiply by the CURRENT health, then add (gain) or subtract (loss).
The potion row starts at 400 health. Find 50% of 400 (0.50 × 400) and ADD it since it's a gain.

optionalActivity.name: Discount Dash Color-by-Code
optionalActivity.intro: Power up your arcade by finding the percent of a number at each Discount Dash stage and matching it to the color code!

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Find the Percent of a Number is multiplying by the percent number itself instead of its decimal form — for example, finding 30% of 80 by computing 30 × 80 = 2,400 instead of 0.30 × 80 = 24. Always divide the percent by 100 to get the decimal, then multiply that decimal by the base.

diagram.title: 12% of 1,500 Tickets Donated
diagram.caption: Each bar is a percent of the 1,500 tickets; 10% is 150, so 12% must be a bit more — 180 tickets, not 18.

connect.scenario: The arcade is donating 12% of Saturday's ticket sales to charity. They sold 1,500 tickets on Saturday. The manager says they will donate 180 tickets. A student says it should be 18 tickets.
connect.promptQuestion: Who is correct, and how do you know?
connect.prompt: The ___ is correct because 12% of 1,500 = ___ × 1,500 = ___. The mistake was ___.

exitTicket.explanation: 45% = 0.45. Multiply: 0.45 × 360 = 162. A student who answers 45 wrote the percent number itself instead of finding the part. A student who answers 315 subtracted the percent number from the base (360 − 45) instead of multiplying. A student who answers 180 rounded 45% up to 50% before multiplying (0.50 × 360). Always convert the exact percent to a decimal, then multiply by the base.
choiceFeedback: Multiply 360 by 0.45 to find 45% of 360.
Find 45% by converting to a decimal and multiplying.
Check: 45% = 0.45, then multiply by 360.
hints: You want 45% OF 360 — a part of 360, so the answer must be less than 360 but not tiny.
Convert 45% to a decimal, then multiply by the base: Part = Percent × Base.
Set up 0.45 × 360. (Shortcut check: 10% of 360 is 36, so 45% is 4.5 of those 36's.)
